Worship

Services & Liturgy

The rhythm of prayer at St. Brendan's — Sunday mornings, midweek quiet, the great feasts, and the sacraments that mark a life.

Sunday morning

Two services. One Sunday.

Our principal services are at 8 and 10 on Sunday morning. Children's Christian formation runs during the 10 o'clock service.

Every Sunday

8:00 AM · Holy Eucharist, Rite I

A spoken service in traditional Prayer Book language. Quiet, reverent, and on the shorter side.

Spoken · ~35 min

What to expect

The full Eucharistic liturgy from Rite I of the 1979 Book of Common Prayer. A brief homily, no music. About a dozen of us, usually, in the front pews. Coffee in the parish hall afterward.

What to wear

Whatever you have on. The 8 o'clock crowd skews toward khakis, jeans, fleece — Maine. The Sunday best is welcome too. Layers are wise; the church is cool in the morning.

Parking

Free in the church lot off Harbor Road and along the street. The harbor lot a block down is also free on Sundays before noon.

Every Sunday

10:00 AM · Choral Eucharist, Rite II

Our principal service. The full Eucharistic liturgy with the parish choir, hymns, sermon, and prayers of the people.

Sung · ~70 min

What to expect

Contemporary Prayer Book language (Rite II), four hymns from the 1982 Hymnal, a sung psalm, and a sermon of about twelve minutes. The choir leads us; we all sing. Communion is shared at the altar rail. Bulletins have everything you need.

What to wear

Anything from sundresses to fishing vests. A few of us wear ties; many don't. Children come as themselves. The point is that you came at all.

Parking & arrival

Come a few minutes early to find a seat and pick up a bulletin. An usher will greet you at the side door. Parking is in the lot and on the street.

Every Sunday during the program year

10:00 AM · Sunday School (ages 3–12)

Children begin in the nave with their families, then process out at the start of the lessons for a story, a craft, and a brief lesson. They return to the nave at the peace, in time for communion.

Sept – mid-June

What we use

A simple Episcopal-friendly curriculum that follows the Sunday lectionary, so the children are hearing the same scriptures we hear upstairs. A teacher and an assistant are on rota each week, both background-checked.

Summer schedule

Sunday School pauses from mid-June through Labor Day. Children stay in the service throughout the summer; a basket of soft toys and quiet books is by the door. Wiggling is allowed.

Nursery

A staffed nursery is open during the 10 AM service for children under three. The room is at the back of the parish hall and is open the whole service.

Weekdays

Quiet, midweek prayer.

Three short services punctuate the week. All are open to anyone; none require any prior knowledge of the Prayer Book.

Every Wednesday

12:10 PM · Healing Eucharist

A spoken Eucharist with prayers for healing and the laying-on of hands. Drop in on your lunch break.

Chapel · ~30 min

For whom

Anyone who would like prayer for healing — for yourself, for someone you love, for grief, for a worry that won't quiet. You may come forward, or remain in your seat.

Format

A short Eucharist using the rite for ministration to the sick, followed by the laying-on of hands and anointing for any who wish it. The Rev. Marcus Adlersson presides.

Where

The side chapel, accessible through the parish hall (the side door off the parking lot). The chapel seats about twenty.

Every Friday

7:00 AM · Morning Prayer

The Daily Office, said together before the day starts. About 25 minutes.

Chapel · ~25 min

What it is

Morning Prayer from the 1979 Book of Common Prayer — psalms, two readings, the canticles, the prayers. A coffee and a quiet hour to begin Friday.

Lay led

Often led by a Licensed Worship Leader from the parish. If you've never said the Office aloud with others, we'll show you the page.

After

A small group often goes for coffee at the Harborline Cafe down the street. You're very welcome to come along.

Every Saturday

5:00 PM · Evening Prayer

The Daily Office at the end of the day, in the candlelit side chapel. About 20 minutes.

Chapel · ~20 min

What it is

Evening Prayer Rite II, with the Phos hilaron sung if there's anyone in the room willing to start the tune. The mood is intentionally simple.

For whom

A handful of regulars; visitors most weeks. Especially loved by those who can't quite manage Sunday morning and want a foothold in the week's prayer.

Summer evensong

From late June through August, Saturday Evening Prayer moves outdoors to the town landing on the third Wednesday of the month — see calendar for dates.

Seasonal liturgies

The great feasts & the great quiet.

The church year shapes what we do. Here are the principal seasonal services — please come, whether or not you're usually with us on Sunday.

Ash Wednesday

Mid-February

Liturgy with the Imposition of Ashes at 12:10 PM and 7:00 PM in the nave. The 7 PM service is sung. Ashes-to-go is offered at the church door from 7 to 9 AM for those who can't attend either liturgy.

Maundy Thursday

Holy Week

7:00 PM. The Eucharist of the Last Supper, with the foot-washing and the stripping of the altar. The Watch in the chapel continues through the night.

Good Friday

Holy Week

12:00 noon — the Good Friday liturgy with the Solemn Collects and the Veneration of the Cross. 7:00 PM — Stations of the Cross, said.

The Great Vigil of Easter

Holy Week

8:00 PM Saturday. We begin in the dark, kindle the new fire on the steps, chant the Exsultet, hear the long history of salvation, and welcome Easter at midnight with the first Eucharist of the resurrection.

Easter Day

Festival

8:00 AM Rite I (spoken) and 10:00 AM Festival Eucharist (with brass, choir, and the children's flowering of the cross). An Easter breakfast is served between the services.

All Saints' Day

November 1 (observed)

10:00 AM Festival Eucharist with the reading of the parish necrology and the baptisms of any candidates being received that day. A reception follows in the parish hall.

Christmas Eve

December 24

4:00 PM — Family Eucharist with a children's pageant (low-key, costumes provided). 10:00 PM — Festival Eucharist with the parish choir, beginning with carols by candlelight at 9:30 PM.

Christmas Day & Epiphany

December · January

10:00 AM Christmas Day Eucharist (spoken, intimate). Epiphany observed on the first Sunday of January with the blessing of chalk for the marking of homes.

Sacraments

Baptism, marriage, burial.

The sacraments mark the great hinges of a life. We are honored to walk with you through them. Please be in touch with the Rector well ahead of the date you have in mind.

Holy Baptism

For infants, children, and adults. Baptisms are normally celebrated within the Sunday Eucharist on one of the four feast days especially appointed for baptism, or whenever a bishop is present.

The four feasts

The Baptism of Our Lord (early January), the Great Vigil of Easter, the Day of Pentecost, and All Saints' Day. We also welcome baptisms at other times when pastorally needed.

Preparation

For an infant or child, one conversation with the Rector and one godparents-and-parents meeting. For adults, a short series of conversations and time spent with the parish community.

To arrange

Contact the Rector at rector@stbrendanskettlecove.org or by calling the parish office.

Holy Matrimony

We celebrate marriages of two people who love one another and intend to make a faithful, lifelong commitment, regardless of gender. At least one of the couple is normally a baptized Christian; one need not be a parishioner, though we hope you'll come and meet us.

Lead time

Six months minimum, often more in summer. The church has weddings June through October; please don't book the reception venue before you've spoken with the Rector.

Preparation

Four conversations with the Rector covering the meaning of the vows, communication, finances, and faith — in addition to your planning of the service itself. We use the marriage rites from the Book of Common Prayer.

To arrange

Write to the Rector. We'll set up a first conversation and walk you through the rest.

Christian Burial

The Burial Office of the Episcopal Church is an Easter liturgy — full of grief, full of hope. We are here for the family of any member of the parish, and for any person in our community whose death calls them here.

What we offer

The Burial Office (Rite I or Rite II), with or without Eucharist. Memorial services may be held weeks or months after the death. Cremation and traditional burial are both welcomed. The parish columbarium is open to members.

In the days after

Please call the parish office — at any hour — when a death occurs. The Rector will come. We will plan with you, simply, in the days that follow. There is no expected donation.

Pre-planning

Many find it a gift to plan their own service ahead of time, choosing hymns and readings. The Rector is glad to help. A simple form is available from the parish office.

If it's your first time

What to expect as a visitor.

Walking into a church for the first time — or for the first time in a long time — can be its own small act of bravery. We'll do our part to make the rest easy.

Where to sit: anywhere except the front-right pew, which Lillian Tasker has occupied since 1987. The ushers at the side door will hand you a bulletin and point you in the right direction; you don't need to know the page numbers, because the bulletin contains every word of the service.

The bulletin is your guide to the morning. Bold text means everyone reads or sings it together; plain text is read by the clergy or the lectors. Hymn numbers refer to the red-bound Hymnal 1982 in the pew rack. When in doubt, follow the person next to you (we all do).

Communion: all baptized Christians of any tradition are welcome to receive the bread and wine at the altar rail. If you would prefer not to receive, you are warmly invited to come forward for a blessing — simply cross your arms over your chest. Gluten-free wafers are available; ask the priest. Children receive at their family's discretion.

Restrooms are off the parish hall (down the side hallway). One is fully accessible. The nave has an accessible entrance from the parking lot, and the side aisle accommodates a wheelchair. A hearing loop covers the front three-quarters of the nave; switch your hearing aid to the T-coil setting.

Children are not a distraction; they are part of the prayer. They will fidget; ours do too. There is a small basket of soft toys and books by the back pew. The nursery is open during the 10 AM service for the very small.

After the service, please come to coffee in the parish hall. The Rector or a Newcomer will find you. We promise not to ambush you with a welcome packet — but there's one available if you'd like it.

The nave, looking east toward the harbor window

Need help planning your visit?

The Newcomers Committee is glad to answer questions ahead of time, save you a seat, or meet you at the door.
